report.tagline: Bharti Airtel's all-in-one app where Airtel customers recharge, pay bills, manage home broadband and TV, claim rewards and get loans, payments and streaming.
report.simpleSummary: Airtel is India's second-largest mobile network. Airtel Thanks is its app: you recharge your phone, pay your postpaid, Wi-Fi or DTH bill, check data, and fix problems. It also gives rewards, like free streaming on Airtel Xstream Play or AI tools, depending on your plan. And it sells money products: Airtel Payments Bank, UPI, loans and credit cards through partners. The idea is simple: if all your Airtel services live in one app with perks, you are less likely to leave Airtel.

overview.whatItDoes: Airtel Thanks is the main customer app for Bharti Airtel in India. It handles prepaid recharges, postpaid and broadband bills, DTH, plan changes and support. It also bundles perks (Thanks rewards), streaming (Xstream Play), finance (Airtel Payments Bank, Airtel Finance loans and partner credit cards) and safety tools like AI spam call alerts.
howItWorks: Users log in with their Airtel number and see all their Airtel connections in one place.
They recharge or pay bills with UPI, cards or Airtel Payments Bank.
Rewards depend on the plan: higher plans unlock things like Xstream Play, Apple Music or AI tool offers.
The app suggests upgrades: from prepaid to postpaid, from one SIM to a family plan, or adding Wi-Fi.
Airtel Finance offers personal loans, gold loans and credit cards from partner lenders inside the app.
Support, SIM issues, porting and complaint tracking are self-service.
overview.valueProposition: One app for every Airtel service, with rewards that make paying more for Airtel feel worth it, and quick fixes without calling customer care.

businessModel.summary: Airtel makes most of its money from mobile plans, then home broadband, business services and DTH. The Airtel Thanks app helps it earn more per user by pushing upgrades and bundles, and adds small new income from loans, cards and payments. Its strategy is to have fewer but higher-paying customers than Jio.

businessModel.pricing: Prepaid plans start around ₹199 to ₹249 for basic validity; popular unlimited 5G plans are around ₹349 to ₹399 for 28 days. Postpaid and Airtel Black family plans are monthly. Exact prices on airtel.in change often.
costDrivers: Content and partner costs for perks
businessModel.unitEconomics: An average Airtel mobile user pays about ₹271 a month, roughly ₹3,250 a year, about ₹50 more a month than a Jio user. The network is a fixed cost, so most extra ARPU becomes profit. A perk that costs Airtel ₹20 to ₹30 a month in partner fees is worth it if it moves a user from a ₹299 plan to a ₹399 plan or stops them leaving. A family on Airtel Black paying mobile plus Wi-Fi might bring ₹1,500 or more a month and leaves far less often.

growth.moat: Airtel's moat is a premium customer base and a national network that is hard and costly to build. The Thanks app strengthens this by bundling many services: a customer with mobile, Wi-Fi, DTH and a loan through Airtel has many reasons not to switch.

pmLessons: A telecom can grow by earning more from each user, not only by adding users.
Bundles reduce churn: the more services a customer has, the harder it is to leave.
Free perks win attention but must be clear; confusing terms turn a gift into a trust problem.
Owning the app gives a direct relationship to cross-sell finance and entertainment.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you reduce Airtel's mobile churn?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment who leaves, why (price, network, offers), design fixes (targeted offers, bundles), measure churn by segment.

interviewQuestions.question: Is giving free AI subscriptions a good idea for Airtel?
interviewQuestions.hint: Cost per user, ARPU lift, brand, trust risks shown by the Perplexity case. Define success metrics.

interviewQuestions.question: What should Airtel Thanks' north star metric be?
interviewQuestions.hint: Customers using two or more Airtel services. Break into app use, services per customer, ARPU, retention.

interviewQuestions.question: Design a feature to sell home Wi-Fi to mobile users.
interviewQuestions.hint: Persona, trigger (high data use at home), offer, one-tap booking. Metric: Wi-Fi attach rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Should Airtel push loans in its app?
interviewQuestions.hint: Benefits (revenue, engagement) vs risks (defaults, trust, regulation). Guardrails like default rate.
